---
title: "sblr"
subtitle: "Scalable Bayesian Linear Regression"
---

`sblr` is an open-source R package for scalable Bayesian linear regression in
genomic prediction, parameter estimation, variable selection, and fine-mapping.

It provides a common framework for:

- scalar-trait and joint multi-trait inference;
- individual-level PLINK BED genotypes;
- GWAS summary statistics and sparse LD;
- retained block-eigen LD representations;
- BayesC, BayesR, and annotation-informed model families;
- deterministic multichain execution;
- canonical posterior, summary, and diagnostic access.

## What `sblr` provides

| Capability | Description |
|---|---|
| Scalar-trait inference | BayesC, BayesR, BayesRC, SBayesC, SBayesR, and SBayesRC-family models |
| Multi-trait inference | General-\(T\) MT-BayesC and factorized pattern-by-scale MT-BayesR |
| Individual-level analysis | Native packed-BED likelihoods without constructing a complete dense cross-product |
| Summary-statistics analysis | Sparse CSR and block-eigen LD operators with explicit approximation semantics |
| Annotation-informed priors | Fixed-marker, grouped, learned-logistic, probit-stick, and log-variance formulations on supported routes |
| MAF-dependent scaling | Explicit `maf_effect_s` control on supported scalar-trait models |
| Reproducible execution | Deterministic logical-task seeds, static scheduling, retention contracts, and worker diagnostics |
| Standardized output | Validated raw results, formatted fits, canonical extractors, posterior summaries, and diagnostics |

::: {.callout-note title="Scientifically specified and validated"}
The public models have explicit likelihood, prior, covariance, state-space,
operator, RNG, retention, and output contracts.

Implementations are exercised using independent numerical references,
analytical reductions, representation comparisons, serial/parallel identity
checks, covariance validation, and focused scientific benchmarks. Validation
establishes the declared implementation contracts; individual analyses still
require suitable chain lengths, diagnostics, sensitivity analysis, and
scientific interpretation.
:::

## Public fitting interfaces

| Interface | Data representation | Model families |
|---|---|---|
| `stblr_bed()` | Individual-level packed BED | BayesC, BayesR, and supported BayesRC models |
| `stblr_csr()` | Summary statistics and sparse CSR LD | SBayesC and SBayesR |
| `stblr_csr_annot()` | Annotation-aware summary statistics and sparse CSR LD | Supported annotation-informed BayesC, BayesR, and BayesRC formulations |
| `stblr_block_eigen()` | Summary statistics and block-eigen LD | Supported SBayesC, SBayesR, SBayesRC, and log-variance models |
| `mtblr_bed()` | Common-sample packed BED | MT-BayesC and factorized pattern-by-scale MT-BayesR |
| `mtblr_csr()` | Independent summary providers with CSR LD | MT-BayesC and factorized pattern-by-scale MT-BayesR |
| `mtblr_block_eigen()` | Independent summary providers with block-eigen LD | MT-BayesC and factorized pattern-by-scale MT-BayesR |

Unsupported model, operator, covariance, or provider combinations fail before
numerical sampling.

## Scalar-trait and multi-trait analysis

The `stblr_*()` interfaces fit scalar-trait models. Multiple scalar traits can
be fitted independently and scheduled in parallel when scientifically
appropriate.

The `mtblr_*()` interfaces fit one joint multi-trait model per logical chain.
They represent shared marker activity, trait-specific activity patterns,
cross-trait effect covariance, and—where supported—full residual covariance.

Analysis mode and execution mode remain distinct:

- independent traits are separate scalar models;
- joint multi-trait analysis is one coupled posterior model;
- traits are not incorrectly treated as independent workers inside a joint
  multi-trait chain.

## Model naming

For scalar-trait model families, the `s` prefix denotes a
summary-statistics likelihood:

| Model | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `bayesc` | Individual-level BayesC |
| `sbayesc` | Summary-statistics BayesC |
| `bayesr` | Individual-level BayesR |
| `sbayesr` | Summary-statistics BayesR |
| `bayesrc` | Individual-level annotation-informed BayesR |
| `sbayesrc` | Summary-statistics annotation-informed BayesR |

Multi-trait interfaces retain the scientific method names `bayesc` and
`bayesr`. Their data representation is determined by the selected
`mtblr_*()` interface.

The `s` prefix is unrelated to `maf_effect_s`. The latter is a separate,
optional MAF-dependent effect-variance scaling control whose value and MAF
provenance are recorded explicitly.

## Shared computational framework

The package reuses common infrastructure across scalar-trait and multi-trait
models:

```text
public fitting interface
→ validated and resolved specification
→ global marker and allele map
→ immutable operator resources and likelihood providers
→ deterministic logical tasks
→ native sampler
→ validated raw result
→ formatted fit
→ canonical extraction, summarization, and diagnostics
```

This separates scientific model semantics from:

- BED decoding;
- CSR and block-eigen operator access;
- provider ownership;
- task scheduling;
- random-number streams;
- retention and convergence capture;
- output formatting.

## LD representations

`sblr` supports three principal data representations:

- packed BED for individual-level analysis;
- sparse CSR LD for summary-statistics analysis;
- block-eigen LD for exact declared block operators and retained-rank
  approximations.

Every operator records its marker order, scale, diagonal, completeness or
approximation status, and provenance. Approximate operators are interpreted
relative to the operator they actually represent; they are not silently
treated as globally exact LD.

See [Data representations](notes/data_representations.qmd) for preparation,
alignment, scaling, and approximation contracts.

## Posterior results and diagnostics

All maintained fits use a common result architecture. Canonical access is
provided through:

```r
extract_posterior()
summarise_posterior()
extract_diagnostics()
```

These functions preserve named trait, chain, marker, component, pattern, and
covariance axes where applicable.

Convergence diagnostics can include:

- rank-normalized R-hat;
- bulk and tail effective sample size;
- Monte Carlo standard error;
- variance and covariance traces;
- probability and annotation parameters;
- selected marker activity and component states.

Diagnostic capture is post-burn-in, unthinned, chain-private, and RNG-neutral.
Diagnostics assess MCMC behavior; they do not by themselves prove model
correctness or universal convergence.

## Project status

`sblr` is actively developed and currently distributed from GitHub. Its public
model semantics, seven fitting interfaces, operator contracts, fit schema, and
canonical access functions are stabilized and tested.

New model families and computational representations are introduced through
explicit design, qualification, and validation checkpoints before public
promotion.
